news.headline: uniQure N.V. Receives Average $65.00 Consensus Price Target From Brokerages
news.summary: Seventeen research firms covering uniQure now carry an average one-year price target of $65.00 and a consensus 'Moderate Buy' rating (13 buys, 3 holds, 1 sell), reflecting continued bullish sentiment following the AMT-130 regulatory clarity and Q2 results.

news.headline: Wolfe Research Upgrades uniQure to Outperform, Sees 'Clear Path to Approval' for AMT-130
news.summary: Wolfe Research upgraded uniQure to Outperform with a $65 price target, arguing the market underestimates AMT-130's approval odds, while Wells Fargo, Leerink and RBC also raised targets (to $75, $70 and $65 respectively) after the Q2 print; Barclays trimmed its target to $60 but kept a Buy rating.

news.headline: UniQure Welcomes Possible AdCom for Huntington's Asset as Regulatory 'Jitters' Spread Through Biopharma
news.summary: On uniQure's Q2 earnings call, chief medical officer Walid Abi-Saab said an FDA advisory committee meeting on AMT-130 is likely and the company is preparing for and welcomes one, even as sector-wide regulatory uncertainty has weighed on gene-therapy peers.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Company Update
news.summary: uniQure reported $810.3 million in cash and investments (runway into 2030) after its June equity raise and confirmed it remains on track to submit the AMT-130 BLA in Q3 2026, alongside a pipeline update noting mid/high-dose AMT-191 (Fabry) dosing remains paused pending liver-enzyme safety review and continued enrollment in the AMT-260 epilepsy trial.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Closing of Upsized Public Offering and Full Exercise by Underwriters of Option to Purchase Additional Shares
news.summary: uniQure closed an upsized public offering of 5,686,813 ordinary shares at $45.50 each, raising roughly $259 million in gross proceeds to fund AMT-130 commercialization readiness, a confirmatory study, and other pipeline programs.

news.headline: uniQure Provides Regulatory Update on AMT-130 for Huntington's Disease
news.summary: Following an FDA Type B meeting, uniQure said the agency agreed the existing 3-year Phase I/II data could serve as the primary basis for an accelerated-approval BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease; shares surged roughly 78% on the news.

catalysts.label: US BLA submission for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to submit the Biologics License Application for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease under the FDA's accelerated approval pathway, with a request for priority review.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing application (MAA) filing
catalysts.detail: Following a successful pre-submission meeting, uniQure plans to file a UK Marketing Authorisation Application for AMT-130 in the same quarter as the US BLA.

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 Phase I/II data
catalysts.detail: Full four-year follow-up data on all 24 patients (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose) from the pivotal Huntington's disease study, to be included in the regulatory package.

catalysts.label: Initiation of AMT-130 confirmatory (Phase 3) study
catalysts.detail: Company plans to start the post-marketing confirmatory trial required alongside the accelerated approval pathway once the BLA is submitted.

catalysts.label: Potential FDA advisory committee (AdCom) meeting on AMT-130
catalysts.detail: Management expects the FDA will likely convene an advisory committee to review AMT-130 given it would be the first approved therapy for Huntington's disease; uniQure says it welcomes and is preparing for one.

catalysts.label: FDA decision on AMT-130 BLA
catalysts.detail: If the Q3 2026 BLA filing is accepted for priority review, an approval decision could arrive within roughly six to twelve months of submission.

pulse: uniQure remains in a strongly bullish stretch following the FDA's June 2026 agreement that existing 3-year AMT-130 data can support an accelerated-approval BLA for Huntington's disease, with Wall Street responding via a wave of price-target increases (Wolfe, Wells Fargo, Leerink, RBC) and a consensus target now around $65. The company closed a $259 million equity raise in late June, extending its cash runway into 2030, reported Q2 2026 results on track for a Q3 BLA filing, and is now preparing for a likely FDA advisory committee review while AMT-191 (Fabry) dosing stays paused pending a safety review. Sentiment is decisively positive, though the AdCom outcome and ultimate BLA decision remain the key swing factors for the stock.
